items.title: Chubby Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: I never was that attracted to a bass solo, until I first heard Jimmy Blanton play.

ctx.x: You know, so somebody was hip to what you were doing.

Well it was very important to me. See my mother was in vaudeville for 42 years. My real father died at an age of 29, he was in a Broadway show at the Wintergarden Theater in New York called “A Girl From Brazil.” So I came from a family of performers. But I loved the actual growth of improvisational music. I was so in love and in awe of everybody. But I also knew that in order to gain attention, I had to do something, because bass solos at that time were not quite as audible. There was no amplifier. And bass solos…
You mean from the All-American Rhythm section.
